title: Retelling from another viewpoint

match.reason: The bank point explains ideas and how point of view shapes what readers know, but it does not teach transforming a story by retelling it from another viewpoint, changing its ending or moving it into a new form.

draft.title: Retelling from another viewpoint
card: A retelling changes a story on purpose. A writer can tell it from a different character's view, change the ending, or move it into a new form, such as a diary entry or a script.
Changing who tells the story changes what the reader knows and feels. A character sees only some events, and has their own reasons and opinions.
Changing the ending changes the message. A story that ends in a reunion leaves a different idea behind than one that ends in a goodbye.
Moving a story into a new form changes how it is told. A text message chat gives short, quick lines. A diary entry gives private thoughts.
draft.remember: Each change in a retelling is a choice, and each choice changes the meaning for the reader.

a.q: A class retells a fairy tale from the wolf's view, so that readers hear his reasons. What is the main effect of this change?
opts: It shows events and motives that the original left out
It changes the story into a different text form
It gives the story a happier ending for every character
It makes the story shorter by removing the other characters
a.why: Telling the story through the wolf lets readers see what he thinks and wants, so the meaning shifts. The form and the ending are not what changed here.
a.clue: Think about who is now telling the story.

b.q: Tariq rewrites a story about a lost dog as a series of short text messages between two friends. Which choice has he made?
opts: He has moved the story into a new form
He has changed the story's ending
He has told it from the dog's viewpoint
He has added a new setting to the story
b.why: Text messages are a different form from a story told in paragraphs, so Tariq has changed form. Two friends are chatting, but nothing says the dog is the one telling it, so viewpoint is not the change.
b.clue: Look at how the story is now presented, not who is in it.

a.best: It shows events and motives that the original left out

b.best: He has moved the story into a new form
